overall: The draft is solid overall: the checker passes 257/257, all 82 tokens are covered, and the token classes are right except 'huana' (Tehuana is too rare; reclassify as exclusive). The biggest systematic problem is repeated facts across sibling tokens: nicotine (cigarettes/smoking/smokers), lung cancer and lungs, pharmacist (dispens/dispensary/medications), Prohibition 1933 and Netherlands 2001 (legalization/legalized), the Hash House Harriers, CB radio and cornerback (' CB'/'CB'), Mariupol and ancient Mari (' Mari'/'Mari'). For the unspaced acronyms (CBD, CBN, CB), the token is often a decorative gloss after the full name, e.g. 'Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN)', so the item doesn't depend on it. Drop the expansion so the acronym is the cue. Quoting person and city names ('Cannavaro', 'Mariupol', 'Maribor') and phrasings like 'Detectors of smoke', 'smoking fumes' and 'to have legalized' are forced. Several answers are given away by the question (Tamarindus/Tamarind, Spanish paprika/Spain, 256-bit/SHA-256, COPD expansion, tetrahydrofolate/folic acid, nicotine patches/nicotine), and some distractor sets are absurd (FIFA/UNESCO/OPEC, noble gases in smoke, Money/shopping bag). On neutrality: the terpene/limonene items and the Syd Barrett psychedelic item lean on cannabis-culture knowledge. Keep the legalization, hydroponics and dispensary items strictly general. Template repetition (four 'X sativa = which crop' items, three Opium Wars items, three 'tetra = four' answers) also needs variety.
